stem: Which one of the following is not related to the Rigvedic period?
expl: Ghosha, Apala, and Vishvavara are all female of hymns or mantras in the Rigveda, and are therefore considered to belong to the Rigvedic era. In contrast, Gargi is a philosopher of the post-Vedic/Upanishadic era, not the Rigvedic era.

stem: Which city served as the capital of the ancient kingdom of Magadha during the early Vedic period?
expl: During the Early Vedic period, Rajagriha (present-day Rajgir) served as the capital of the ancient Magadha empire. The first dynasty of Magadha was the Brihadratha dynasty. Brihadratha is mentioned in the Rigveda.

stem: Which Mandala of the Rig Veda is completely dedicated to ‘Soma’?
expl: There are a total of 10 Mandalas in the Rigveda. All 114 hymns (suktas) of the Ninth Mandala are dedicated to Soma. Soma was the main drink of the Aryans, which was obtained from the Mujavant peak. In the Tenth Mandala of the Rigveda, the origin of the four varnas is mentioned.

stem: Gayatri Mantra is found in which book?
expl: The Gayatri Mantra is mentioned in the Rigveda. Its composer is Vishwamitra. This mantra is described in the Third Mandala of the Rigveda. It is dedicated to Savitr (the Sun deity).

stem: In which phase was the concept of untouchability was clearly put?
expl: In the period of the Dharmashastras (during the Sutra period), apart from the four varnas (Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra), many other castes also emerged in society—such as Ambashtha, Ugra, Nishad, Magadh, Vaidehak, Rathakar, etc.—as a result of anuloma and pratiloma marriages. Panini mentioned two types of Shudras—Niravasita and Aniravasita. Among these, the first type of Shudras was considered untouchable.

stem: When did the use of iron begin in the Indian subcontinent?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: There are differences of opinion among scholars about the beginning of iron use in the Indian subcontinent. Some scholars believe that the Hittites were the first in the world to begin using iron, and only after that did its use spread to other countries. However, excavations at the Ban Chiang archaeological site in Thailand have yielded cast iron, dated approximately to 1600–1200 BCE. In India, iron has been found from the Doab area of Noh (Rajasthan) along with Black-and-Red Ware, and its probable date is considered around 1400 BCE. The earliest clear references to this metal are found in texts of the Later Vedic period (about 1000–600 BCE.). In the Atharvaveda, iron is mentioned as “Shyama Ayas” (dark metal), and there is also a reference to an iron ploughshare. Excavations at Atranjikhera (Uttar Pradesh) have yielded the earliest agricultural iron tools along with remains of wheat, barley, and rice. Archaeologists have dated it to around 1000 BCE., which is accepted by most scholars.

stem: Famous Battle of ‘Ten Kings’ was fought on the bank of the river:
expl: The Dasarajna War (Battle of Ten Kings) was fought on the bank of the Parushni River (modern Ravi River), in which Sudas, the king of the Bharatas, won.

stem: Which ancient Indian text, composed during the Later Vedic period, contains philosophical hymns and discussions on cosmology and ethics?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The Upanishads, composed during the Later Vedic period, include philosophical dialogues and discussions on cosmology and ethics. The Upanishads are ancient Indian texts written in Sanskrit, roughly between 700 BCE. and 300 BCE.
